description: How the global coffee giants rose — and how a Chinese challenger blasted to the top before collapsing. Market caps, scandals and comeback plays across 20 years of coffee capitalism.
youtube_description:
The Coffee Conquest — a chart race that tells the caffeine-fueled story of the global coffee market. Watch Nestlé's long dominance, Starbucks' meteoric expansion, the 2019–2020 Luckin boom-and-bust, and how legacy players like McDonald's and JDE Peet's tracked steady growth. Every spike and crash here maps to real events: IPOs, global expansion, COVID shocks, the Luckin accounting scandal (2020) and the consolidation plays that followed.

Why this matters: coffee is daily culture for billions and a multibillion-dollar battleground for brand, retail footprint and supply chain control. This visualization shows who won shelf space, who bought brands, who got hit by scandal — and who came out richer.

Sources: public market-cap filings, IPO disclosures, company annual reports and market coverage (years 2007–2026). If you want a breakdown by revenue, store count, or regional split (China vs US vs EMEA), drop a comment — I’ll make a follow-up.

Subscribe for weekly chart races and deep-dive explainers. Like, comment which coffee chain surprised you most, and share to wake up your feed.
